text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 2287654321 — Streaming p99 tail latency spike detected on /v1/streaming/generate (eu-west-2). p50=95ms p95=520ms p99=2.4s. Multiple streaming stalls and TLS handshake retries observed across azb->azc. Alert threshold breached: SLO (p99 < 1s). Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/streaming-overview -> alert#2287654321

maya_oncall: acknowledged, I'm on it. paging liam_sre and priya_net. starting initial triage. @jenna_support can you start a customer impact note? :eyes:

liam_sre: oncall here. checking recent deploys first — any rollout in eu-west-2 in the last 30m?

priya_net: no deploys from infra. Seeing network anomalies in NAT metrics for eu-west-2 NAT-A. forwarding host-level conntrack counts to chat.

liam_sre: paste p99 series and top error rates please. also paste any tcp retransmit / packetloss graphs.

priya_net: metrics snippet:
```
Region: eu-west-2
Endpoint: /v1/streaming/generate
window: 10m
p50: 95ms
p95: 520ms
p99: 2.4s
streaming stalls: 7.8% connections saw stall > 500ms
client-visible timeouts: 1.9%
NAT translations used: 65534 / 65534 (94% over last 5m)
TLS handshakes retries: +430% vs baseline
packet loss (inter-az): p99 3.7%
```

maya_oncall: NAT translations at 65k.. that smells like ephemeral exhaustion. @priya_net can you confirm which NAT gateway and whether it's a managed cloud NAT or self-hosted?

priya_net: it's cloud-nat gw-id nat-0a1b2c3d eu-west-2a/2b/2c. translations look saturated across all AZs; rate of new TCP ephemeral allocations spiked ~00:05 UTC. suspect backends are short-lived client conns (streaming shims) creating many outbound connections.

liam_sre: ok. quick mitigation options: 1) scale NAT (add additional NAT gateway / increase throughput) 2) route critical streaming egress via a fallback NAT in eu-west-1 3) apply ephemeral port reuse + adjust conntrack (short-term) 4) enable smart-routing fallback to us-west-1 for non-sensitive tenants.

jenna_support: customer impact: preliminary — ~2% of streaming requests timed out or stalled; top affected customers: alpha-co (2% of their calls), beta-inc (1.7%). ETA for official note: 15m once we stabilize. Should we open a status page incident?

erin_prod: yes please. mark incident P1 and add "partial streaming degradation - cross-zone egress NAT saturation". Customer comms should say intermittent stalls and elevated latency; working on routing fix.

liam_sre: I'm going to attempt an immediate traffic reroute for the streaming route to hit dedicated NAT-B in eu-west-2 and add an extra NAT in eu-west-1 as fallback. Priya — can you prep the routing change? I'll coordinate with infra team.

priya_net: starting now. applying route override to streaming-route via gateway nat-0d9e8f7 (eu-west-2b) and opening a temporary transit to eu-west-1 nat-0f1e2d3c.

liam_sre: running quick health checks after route change — collecting tcpdump (sampling 1%) on streaming egress for 30s.
```
# on jumpbox
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/stream-sample.pcap port 443 and host 10.12.34.56 -c 10000
# samples: 10000 packets captured, retransmits spiked then dropped
```

priya_net: routing change applied at 00:12:25 UTC. NAT-B accepted ~20k translations immediately. monitoring.

maya_oncall: update: p95 dropped from 520ms to ~220ms in first 60s; p99 trending down but still ~1.1s. streaming-stall rate down from 7.8% -> 2.6% in first 2m.

liam_sre: good. I'm also flushing conntrack entries on the streaming nodes where safe to do so, to free TIME_WAIT entries. Doing one AZ at a time. Command:
```
sudo conntrack -F && sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
```

priya_net: note: increasing conntrack_max helps long-term but doesn't free ephemeral ports; need NAT capacity. scaling additional NAT as planned. opening request to infra to provision 2x NAT gateways now.

jenna_support: drafting customer status update: "We're investigating elevated streaming latency and stalls in eu-west-2. We've applied traffic reroutes and are scaling network translation capacity; some customers may see intermittent stalls while we stabilize. Further updates in 15 minutes." Anyone object?

erin_prod: good. include link to support channel and mention affected endpoints. :+1:

liam_sre: infra reports second NAT created and attached at 00:14:40 UTC. We now have 3 NATs serving streaming egress. translation usage dropped to 45% across pool. p99 now at ~700ms and trending downward.

maya_oncall: traffic mostly stable. TLS handshake retry rate down ~70%. marking "working" in incident doc. tagging page to follow with RCA for root cause (applications creating many short-lived outbound connections causing ephemeral exhaustion across NAT pool and cross-zone routing magnified packet re-transmits).

priya_net: putting temporary guardrails: enable long-lived connections for streaming clients where possible, recommend keepalive and connection reuse in SDKs. Also will roll out a per-tenant egress quota to protect shared NAT resources.

liam_sre: planning post-incident action items: 1) increase default NAT pool capacity and automation to scale proactively 2) enhance egress telemetry (per-tenant nat usage) 3) SDK changes for connection reuse 4) run chaos tests for cross-az NAT failure 5) update runbooks for conntrack/NAT exhaustion.

jenna_support: customer note sent at 00:18 UTC. responses: alpha-co replied "saw reconnects but now stable", beta-inc awaiting follow-up. I'll queue post-incident customer writeups.

maya_oncall: handing off to next oncall: jenna_support will take monitoring for 1 hour, liam_sre and priya_net can be paged if regressions appear. I'm logging initial incident ticket: INC-2026-1932.

jenna_support: ack. I'll watch dashboards and notify if p99 > 1s for 5 consecutive minutes. setting on-call reminder.

liam_sre: closing mitigation: traffic reroute + additional NATs + conntrack flush kept latency within SLO for now. Will follow up with RCA.

maya_oncall: incident status -> mitigated at 00:20:21 UTC. final metrics snapshot: p50 90ms p95 180ms p99 420ms, stall rate 0.9%, TLS retry rate +10% (near baseline).

priya_net: capturing all logs and packet captures to incident S3: s3://incidents/2287654321/pcaps/ and starting retention job.

jenna_support: postmortem owner? liam_sre volunteer?

liam_sre: I'll own the RFC and postmortem. timeline + action items in doc.

maya_oncall: thanks team. closing thread for now — will reopen if regression. :white_check_mark:
